text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Norwegian papers this morning.

- A fusion between Norway's largest insurer Storebrand and commercial bank Christiania Bank og Kreditkasse is not necessarily an advantage for their customers, a state researcher concludes. The two companies proposed plans to merge on Tuesday.
- Finance Minister Jens Stoltenberg will not yet guarantee that he will support a merger between Storebrand an Christiania Bank. He says it is up to the government to make a final decision.
- Six out of ten pupils think school is boring and dull. The Norwegian school system is more advantageous to girls and stops boys from fully using their abilities, a researcher says.

- The proposed merger between Christiania Bank and Storebrand could meet opposition from shareholders. On Wednesday afternoon after the merger announcement a large block of preference shares in Storebrand, corresponding to 2.6 percent of the voting stock was sold. That block could weigh heavily in the battle over the fusion.
- Norway is at the top of a list of countries for people completing higher education. However, the OECD recomends that Norway put more emphasis on vocational training.

- The Russian and Ukrainian mafia want to stop Norsk Hydro from operating in Ukraine. Hydro's partner in Ukraine has recieved threats, while Hydro has partly lost ownership of an important chemical import and export terminal at Yuzhnyy.
